A.instructions: Does the text say which company or body conducted the poll?
Does the text give the address or seat of the pollster?
Does the text say who commissioned or funded the poll?
Does the text say how many people were interviewed?
Does the text state a margin of error for the poll?
Does the text state the confidence level of the margin of error?
Does the text state which population the poll represents?
Does the text explain the sampling system?
Does the text explain how respondents were selected or contacted?
Does the text say how the interviews were conducted?
Does the text state the fieldwork dates?
Does the text reproduce the exact wording of the questions?
Does the text state how many people did not answer each question?
Does the text mention that data were weighted?
Does the text refer to a technical sheet published elsewhere?

B.instructions: What kind of survey does the text describe?

criteria.voting_intention_estimate: a model or seat estimate derived from polls
criteria.direct_voting_intention: respondents stated which party they would vote for
criteria.issue_opinion: opinion on issues, not voting intention
criteria.self_selected_online_poll: open online vote by readers, self-selected

B.instructions: Is the text about voting intention or election results?
Does the text present results as a prediction of the election outcome rather than a snapshot?
Does the headline or lede present one party as clearly ahead or winning?
How much does the headline claim beyond what the data in the text support?
Does the text present small-subgroup results as if they held for the whole population?

C.instructions: Does the wording of the question push towards a concrete answer?
Does the question use evaluative or emotional terms about any option?
